text:
In the foliage, green case that gold gilds,

in the foliage, uncertain and clotted with flowers

that bloom magnificent, where a kiss dwells,

nervous, while tearing the splendid embroideries,


a frightened faun arches his brow,

biting the red flowers with his white teeth.

Dark, stained with blood, like aged wine,

his lip bursts into laughter, lost among leaves.


And when, like a squirrel, through the fronds he is startled,

caught on the branches his laughter shivers;

and we see, frightened by the singing chaffinch,

how the golden Kiss of the Forest falls asleep.

translation.title: Head of a Faun
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the faun's leafy emergence and the forest kiss falling asleep.
